title: Livewire 2.2: Undefined variable slot in app.blade.php

content:
# Livewire 2.2: Undefined variable slot in app.blade.php If you are working with Laravel Livewire 2.2, encountering an "Undefined variable: slot" error is a classic symptom of how the framework handles component rendering contexts. The error message specifically points to `layouts/app.blade.php`, indicating that the layout template itself is being parsed before Livewire has fully initialized its own rendering context for the specific component you are trying to load. This issue arises when using the `@livewire` directive inside a Blade view that extends a layout containing `{{ $slot }}`. In your scenario, the route works perfectly fine because it renders the component directly without an intervening layout layer. However, when you extend `layouts.app`, the rendering flow changes subtly but critically. The root cause lies in the interaction between Livewire's component rendering stack and Laravel's Blade compilation order. When you call `@livewire('my-livewire-component')` within a view that extends `layouts.app`, Blade attempts to resolve the content passed to the layout. If `layouts.app` contains `{{ $slot }}`, it expects a variable named `$slot` to be available in the data array passed to the layout. In Livewire 2.x, when rendering a component via the `@livewire` directive, the framework does not automatically inject content into the `$slot` of the parent layout unless explicitly configured to do so. The `@livewire` directive generates its own output and places it directly into the view stream. However, if the layout is set up to expect `$slot` (which is standard practice for layouts), and Livewire's internal rendering logic doesn't bridge that gap in version 2.2, the variable remains undefined at parse time. To resolve this without upgrading Livewire, you must ensure that the layout does not rely on an existing `$slot` value when Livewire components are being rendered via the directive. The most direct fix involves modifying `layouts/app.blade.php`. Instead of relying on a dynamic `$slot`, you can explicitly render the content or bypass the slot mechanism for this specific context. One effective approach is to remove `{{ $slot }}` from `layouts/app.blade.php` if your layout does not need to support multiple slots dynamically in this specific use case. Alternatively, you can pass an empty string or a dummy value to satisfy Blade's parser: ```blade @livewireStyles
{{ $slot ?? '' }}
@livewireScripts ``` However, the more robust solution in Livewire 2.2 involves checking how the component is being invoked. When you use `Route::get('/path', ComponentClassPath)`, Laravel renders the component directly, bypassing the layout entirely. This means no `$slot` logic is required because there is no parent layout expecting content injection. The discrepancy occurs only when using `@livewire('my-livewire-component')` inside a blade file that extends a layout with `$slot`. In Livewire 2.2, the directive does not automatically populate `$slot` in the parent layout unless you are using the newer component syntax or have updated dependencies. If you need to maintain the layout structure and support multiple components, consider moving the `@livewire` directive outside of the slot context or ensuring your layout explicitly handles the Livewire rendering stack. Another option is to use the `Livewire\Features\SupportComponentSlot` class if available in your version, though this is more common in newer versions. In practice, many developers find that upgrading to a later version of Livewire resolves this ambiguity, as subsequent versions improved how components interact with layout slots. If you are locked into Laravel 7.24 and Livewire 2.2 due to compatibility constraints, the safest immediate workaround is to avoid using `@livewire` inside layouts that rely on `$slot`. Instead, render the component directly in the blade file without extending a layout, or modify the layout to not use `$slot` when rendering Livewire components via the directive. Understanding these rendering contexts prevents future confusion when integrating Livewire with complex layout structures. Always verify whether your layout expects a `$slot` variable before invoking Livewire directives that may not inject content into it automatically in older versions.
